_about: THE GLOSSARY, written once (the component plan's C3 and C9, approved 9 October 2026): the record's shorthand, each term with its name in full and what it means. components.py reads this file and the build writes it into site/components.js, between the WORDBOOK markers, as WORDBOOK.glossary. A key starting with '_' is a note and goes to neither.

NOTHING DRAWS THESE YET. The term popovers come in the component plan's step 6: a writer in either language marks a term <span data-term="ITL">, choosing the key by context -- RC is a roll call on a vote and the Regular Calendar in a committee's report, so the second is keyed RC-calendar -- and components.js makes the first on the page a button that opens its entry, on a tap, a hover held about half a second or keyboard focus, staying while the pointer moves onto it and closing on Escape (WCAG 1.4.13; the person, 9 October 2026). FN, A and LOCAL are the suffixes on a bill's number.

THE WORDS ARE THE SITE'S OWN, as already published, and 'from' says where: Learn's 'Using this site' (its table 'Reading the shorthand'), 'How a bill becomes law' (its table under 'How committees work'), the vote words the person approved on 8 October 2026 (only OTP, OTPA, ITL and IS are spelled as abbreviations on a vote), and the General Court's own docket key (records/docket_abbrev.json). 'says' is empty where the source gives the name alone.

OTP.name: Ought to Pass
OTP.says: a motion to pass the bill

IS.name: Interim Study
IS.says: second year only, and the bill dies with the term

Retain.name: Retain
Retain.says: Hold the bill in the committee — first year only, and it returns in the second

CC.name: Consent Calendar
CC.says: the committee's recommendation, to pass, to kill or to send to interim study, adopted with the whole calendar in one vote, without floor debate

HJ.name: House Journal
HJ.says: the chamber's own record of the day, cited by issue and sometimes page

SJ.name: Senate Journal
SJ.says: the chamber's own record of the day, cited by issue and sometimes page

FN.name: Fiscal note
FN.says: an estimate of what the bill would cost
